reason: Fire is the obvious means of lighting the cave's interior.
expectation: The fire will light the sheltered cave for painting.

effect: The fire lit the cave wall and revealed a goal to paint an animal from memory.
reaction: The lit wall gives the painting task a clear place to happen.
reason: Weathered rock can contain pigments, and water may help turn them into paint.
expectation: The rock and water will make a usable pigment or paint.

effect: The rock and water made pigment suitable for marking the cave wall.
reason: The pigment belongs on the lit cave wall; memory may also be needed to depict the animal.
expectation: The pigment will be used to paint on the wall, perhaps drawing on memory.

effect: The pigment and memory produced an animal painting, revealing a goal to add stars.
reaction: The remembered animal made the painting feel purposeful.
reason: Stars are available and the new goal asks to add them to the painting.
expectation: Stars will be added to the cave painting.

effect: The cave painting now includes stars, completing that goal; making a song remains.
reaction: The image now brings the animal and night sky together.
reason: A call is a vocal sound, and memory could help people repeat it as a song; this is a guess.
expectation: The remembered call may become a song or a step toward one.

effect: The call could not combine with memory, but automatically produced an echo in the sea cave.
reaction: The echo is a useful and unexpected acoustic step toward the song.
reason: The echo may have several possible uses, so checking its partners should clarify how it contributes to the song.
expectation: The compatibility report will show what can be combined with the echo, possibly to make a song.

effect: The echo combined automatically with memory to make a song, revealing the goal of passing on knowledge.
reaction: It is satisfying that remembering and repeating the echo produced a song.
reason: Shared discovery represents knowledge the community can pass on, and the song can be taught to others.
expectation: The community will use the song to pass on what it has learned.

effect: Song has no available combination, so I need another way to pass on the community's knowledge.
reaction: I was surprised the song could not be used for teaching.
reason: A story can convey the shared discovery to other people.
expectation: The community will pass on its discovery through a story.

alternatives.reason: Checking its partners could clarify how the knowledge is passed on.

effect: Story and shared discovery produced teaching, completing the chapter's final goal.
reaction: The emphasis on explaining a prediction and letting others practise made the ending concrete.

mostWorthwhile.text: Making the echo and turning it into a song linked reflected sound to a repeatable rhythm in a memorable way.

leastWorthwhile.text: Trying to use the finished song for teaching led nowhere, despite the song's description saying it could be taught.

surprise.text: The failed call-and-memory guess automatically revealed the cave echo, which then became the basis for the song.

arbitrary.text: Using memory to turn an echo into a song was evocative, but the specific pairing was not obvious to me until I inspected the echo.

continue.text: Yes. I would be curious to see more combinations connect physical phenomena with human creativity, especially when their explanations are as concrete as the echo and teaching passages.
